newsitem.title: BULGARIA: EBRD to resume Bulgaria investment after IMF deal.
newsitem.headline: EBRD to resume Bulgaria investment after IMF deal.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said on Wednesday it was prepared to resume investing in Bulgaria after the government signs an agreement with the International Monetary Fund.
"We are ready to support the banking sector once the government has an agreement with the IMF," EBRD Sofia resident representative Tim O'Neill told reporters.

An IMF technical mission is currently in Sofia to prepare discussions for a negotiation mission expected to arrive on Monday. The IMF will resume talks on the implementation of a fixed exchange rate regime expected to stabilise the crumbling financial system.

Speaking after a meeting with interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski, O'Neill said there were projects in the pipeline which then could result in EBRD committing between $100 million and $200 million.
An interim cabinet led by Sofianski took office last week inherting from the former Socialist government, largely composed of communists, complete economic chaos.
The Socialists bowed to 30 days of mass protests, agreeing last week to hold elections on April 19, almost two years before the end of their term.

"We are prepared to support the banking system through privatsations, through support of private sector banks and look forward to the stabilisation that will follow the implementation of a currency board," said O'Neill.
The bank revised its funding strategy for Bulgaria last year after delayed reforms deterred development of the private sector.

Delayed structural reform, a weak and poorly functioning banking system, corruption and a slow and reluctant privatisation has led to Sofia's failure to meet a 60/40 private/public portfolio requirement which is due by June 1997.
The EBRD has approved 21 investments totalling 215.5 million European Currency Units in the financial sector, agribusiness, transportation, telecommunications, energy insurance and consumer goods.
Eighteen percent of the signed projects are in the private sector. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
